But in a production as good as this one by Sam Yates and with a forceful central performance by Josh O’Connor as Joe Bonaparte, violinist turned boxer in Depression-era America, it makes its case as a powerful, admonitory slice of theatre noir.

O’Connor doesn’t pull his punches as he takes on the role of Joe Bonaparte, an ambitious and gifted violinist from an Italian American family, who abandons his true musical passions in favour of the fame and riches of boxing.
The last 20 minutes go slightly off the rails as the production's melodramatic denouement resorts to explosive bursts of shouting and recrimination following a bloody and tragic bout.

cn.t: O'Connor's stage return electrifies this rare Odets revival, with critics praising the ensemble cast and punchy direction. Some find the 1937 play clunky and melodramatic, but most agree the production's bold staging overcomes the dated material.
